title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten page (numbered 167 in the cote) written on the back of a reused typescript. The visible typescript, also shown as the 'neighbouring pages', is Grothendieck's SGA 7 Exp. IX (monodromy, Weil eigenvalues, local conductor of abelian schemes), pp. 362-363. The handwritten text belongs to the notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture on a de Rham complex with divided powers.

Goal of the page: describe all morphisms between two 'universal' objects. The source is A_k = A(k{T}, k{T}^+, T), attached to the divided-power (PD) polynomial algebra k{T} over k, its augmentation PD-ideal k{T}^+ and the variable T. The target is the analogous A_{k'} over k'. These objects are differential rings of some combinatorial type ('anneaux diff. ½-pliciaux'; reading uncertain, perhaps semi-simplicial or cosimplicial). Grothendieck reduces the morphisms to explicit data in PD-polynomial algebras.

Step (1)(b). The image φ0(T) must lie in the PD-ideal S'^+. It is otherwise unconstrained, apart from what condition 2) imposes. An earlier attempt writing φ0(T) = Σ η'_i T^{(i)} is crossed out.
NB. If one first fixes φ00 : k → k' and requires φ_* (equivalently φ0) to be φ00-semilinear, then datum 1) reduces to (b).

Step (2). A'_1 lies in S'{X_0}, with S' = k'{T}. Identifying T with a second PD variable X_1 gives S'{X_0} ≅ k'{X_0, X_1}, so A'_1 = Σ α_ij X_0^{(i)} X_1^{(j)}. The condition A'_1 ∈ S'{X_0}^{++} means α_{0j} = 0 for all j, i.e. i ≥ 1 throughout. Applying the projection p_{S'} (setting X_1 = 0) gives Σ_{i≥1} α_{i0} T^{(i)}. Hence φ0(T) is not independent data: it is read off from A'_1 as φ0(T) = Σ_{i≥1} α_{i,0} T^{(i)}.

Step (3). The elements B'_i ∈ S'{X_0} (i ≥ 1) are subject only to the 2-torsion conditions (2B'_i)·J = 0.

Corollary 5 (summary). Morphisms A_k → A_{k'} correspond bijectively to triples (φ00, A'_1, (B'_i)_{i≥1}) where:
- φ00 : k → k'{T} is a ring homomorphism;
- A'_1 ∈ k'{T}{X_0}^{++};
- B'_i ∈ k'{T}{X_0}.
They must satisfy:
- a) A'_1 = Σ_{i≥1, j≥0} α'_ij X_0^{(i)} X_1^{(j)};
- b) (2B'_i)·J' = 0, where J' ⊂ S_{k'} = k'{T} is the ideal generated by the coefficients a'_j of A' = Σ_{j≥1} a'_j X_0^{(j)} and the coefficients b'_ij of B'_i = Σ_{j≥0} b'_ij X_0^{(j)}.
Since S{X_0} is free over S on the X_0^{(j)}, b) is equivalent to (b'): (2b'_ij)·J' = 0 for all i ≥ 1, j ≥ 0.

The factor 2 is the characteristic-2 phenomenon typical of divided powers on odd-degree (differential) elements. In a graded-commutative algebra, ω^2 = 2ω^{[2]}, so strict commutativity and PD compatibility interact only through 2-torsion. The page is thus a step in determining the endomorphisms or functoriality ('cooperations') of a universal PD de Rham object, i.e. a computation of a co-representing object.
errors: Possible inconsistency in φ00. The NB treats φ00 as a ring map k → k', but Cor. 5 writes φ00 : k → k'{T}. Either a slip, or in the corollary the semilinearity normalization of the NB is not imposed.

In step (3), J is used before it is defined. In the corollary the ideal J' is generated by coefficients of A'_1 and of the B'_i themselves, so b) is a self-referential (non-linear) condition on the data. That is not wrong, but it should be stated explicitly.

Notational drift. A'_1 (two-variable expansion with α'_ij) and A' (one-variable expansion over k'{T} with coefficients a'_j, j ≥ 1) denote the same element under X_1 ↔ T. Then a'_j = Σ_i α'_{j i} T^{(i)}, which the page does not spell out.
The reduction b) ⇔ b') is correct, because S{X_0} is free over S on the basis X_0^{(j)}. No mathematical error is detected beyond these presentational gaps.

ideas.what: Identification S{X_0} ≅ k'{X_0,X_1} for S = k'{T}: a PD polynomial algebra over a PD polynomial algebra is a PD polynomial algebra in more variables
ideas.modern_name: free divided power algebras / PD envelopes of polynomial algebras

ideas.what: Classification of morphisms between universal PD-differential objects A(k{T}, k{T}^+, T) by explicit data (ring map, an element of the augmentation-squared part, a sequence B'_i) subject to 2-torsion conditions
ideas.modern_name: co-representability / cooperations of a universal divided-power de Rham (Dieudonné-type) algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related later frameworks: Illusie (de Rham–Witt, 1979); Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew (Dieudonné algebras, 2019)

ideas.what: 2-torsion condition (2B)·J = 0 expressing the compatibility of divided powers with odd-degree (differential) elements
ideas.modern_name: strict graded-commutativity in characteristic 2 (x^2 = 0 for odd x) in PD dg-algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in PD dga theory (Cartan; Berthelot–Ogus; Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew impose x^2 = 0 for odd x)

ideas.what: Reduction of datum 1) to the image of T once a semilinear structure over a fixed φ00 : k → k' is required
ideas.modern_name: semilinear morphisms / base change of PD structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes the morphisms between universal 'divided-power de Rham' objects A(k{T}, k{T}^+, T) for varying base rings, including the 2-torsion constraint. This suggests he aimed at a universal or co-representing description of the PD de Rham complex functor. Nothing on this page is visibly continued in the published literature attributed to him; the 1976 IHES lecture itself was never written up.
missed.quote: Cor.5 Les hom. d'anneaux diff/ ½-pliciaux A_{k*} = A(k{T}, k{T}^+, T) → A_{k'*} ... satisfaisant les conditions a) ... b) (2B'_i)J' = 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew's Dieudonné algebras and recent work on co-representability of de Rham–Witt and prismatic functors study exactly such universal objects and their endomorphisms. A 1976 explicit computation, including the characteristic-2 subtlety, is a historical precursor worth noting.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine but careful explicit computation of morphisms between PD-polynomial-based differential algebras. It documents Grothendieck working concretely on a universal PD de Rham object in 1976, a precursor theme to de Rham–Witt and Dieudonné algebras. However, the content shown is elementary bookkeeping, and the larger construction is not visible here.
transcription_corrections: First line: probably 'φ0(T) ∈ S'^+, [soit] mais sinon [non] fixé par condition 2)' rather than 'mais sans fixé'.
'anneaux diff/ ½-pliciaux' is uncertain; possibly 'anneaux diff[érentiels] semi-simpliciaux' or a similar abbreviation.
In Cor. 5 the element is written A'_* / A'_1 with coefficients α'_ij; the first datum reads 'φ00 : k → k'{T} hom. d'anneaux' as transcribed.
The NB line reads approximately: 'si on suppose qu'on se donne d'abord φ = φ00 : k → k', et qu'on exige φ_* φ00-semi-linéaire, i.e. φ0 φ00-semi-linéaire, la donnée 1) se réduit à (b)'.
Before the definition of A' and B'_i there is a crossed-out line, and the next line begins 'où' (not 'on'): 'où A' = Σ a'_j X_0^{(j)} ...'.
The page number at the bottom left reads 167.
